walkthroughs.body_html:
% yield = (actual / theoretical) x 100.

Why less than 100%? Losses, incomplete reactions, side reactions.

AE = (Mr of useful product / Mr of all products) x 100.

Higher AE = less waste = greener industry.

Increase pressure: shifts to fewer gas moles.

Increase temperature: shifts in endothermic direction.

mcqs.q: If forward reaction is exothermic, raising temperature shifts equilibrium:
options: right
left
no shift
depends on pressure

mcqs.q: Does a catalyst affect the position of equilibrium?
options: No — it speeds up both the forward and reverse reactions equally, so equilibrium is reached faster but at the same position.
A catalyst increases the yield by being consumed in the forward reaction only.
A catalyst shifts the equilibrium towards the products.
Different gases occupy completely different volumes proportional to their molar mass.

mcqs.q: What does a mole of a substance represent?
options: Different gases occupy completely different volumes proportional to their molar mass.
A mole is a unit of mass equal to the relative molecular mass in grams of any substance.
Avogadro's number (6.02 x 10^23) of particles of that substance.
A mole is a unit of volume equal to 24 dm^3 at any temperature.

mcqs.q: At room temperature and pressure, what volume does 1 mole of any gas occupy?
options: A catalyst increases the yield by being consumed in the forward reaction only.
Different gases occupy completely different volumes proportional to their molar mass.
Heavier gases occupy a smaller volume per mole because their particles are denser.
Approximately 24 dm^3 (24,000 cm^3), regardless of the identity of the gas.
